data.claim: Wall-time metrics for gates, ci, review, queue wait, cycle time and rework exist and are log-derived (ddflow metrics); per-process CPU/rss/io/network, per-test time, tool-call counts, token cost per task and flaky rate are not measured anywhere; phase id P-perf already exists (log read path, hook latency, import time).
data.falsifier: A grep finding resource.getrusage, psutil or per-test duration capture in ddflow/, or an event kind recording cpu/rss/io, would refute the gap claim; ddflow metrics showing per-test times would too.
data.mechanism: Gate/ci/review events carry evidence.elapsed_s and waited_s (services/gates/runner.py, ci.py, infra/proc.py run_shell monotonic); services/metrics/* folds them; flowsignals and infra/signals.py sample load, memory, disk to .ddflow/local/flow/samples.jsonl via ticks.py. No getrusage/psutil anywhere in ddflow/ or tests/ (grep). Cadence passes are a fixed table COUNT_PASSES in services/schedule.py plus [cadence] knobs and prompts in templates/prompts/commands; P-observe.telemetry/.detectors/.experiments, B-perf-bench, B-gap-spend, ETA-data, SCH-review-inbox already plan much of the rest.
data.probe: ddflow metrics; grep -rIn 'ru_maxss\|getrusage\|psutil' ddflow tests; log scan of gate.passed/failed evidence keys for unit_tests and ci
data.probe_output: metrics: ci n=2251 p50 8m p90 24m, critic p50 7m, unit_tests p50 10m, cycle p50 1.2h; grep: no matches; evidence keys: elapsed_s 2731, waited_s 173, workers 49, no cpu/rss/io keys; ci passed count 5737-12042 (early Oct) to 16141 (late Oct), median elapsed 460 s flat
data.question: What does ddflow already measure or plan about performance, and what is missing for a metrics-collection and periodic-analysis phase?
